hinge.title: Interpret graphs with a two-step process: first identify axes, units, scale, legend, categories, and visible patterns, then make only conclusions justified by those observations.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Units is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Interpret graphs with a two-step process: first identify axes, units' is answered as units rather than axes.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: axes still holds here even though Approximate graph values should be tied to the displayed scale and markings is missing from the stem — on the item about Interpret graphs with a two-step process: first.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Units is what produces axes, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Interpret graphs with a two-step process: first.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The axes rule also covers this: causal explanations for graph trends, so it is not an exception — on the item about Interpret graphs with a two-step process: first.

intelligence.enrichment: When graphs contain a lot of information, interpretation is simplified by first identifying how the graph is organised and what patterns it shows, then analysing those observations to make summary and conclusion statements that the data supports.
